int dlmulti (  char *  name,
char *  file,
int  flag,
void **  libr,
const char *  fmt,
  ...
) 
 

satisfy symbols from a shared object.

dlopen() on steroids. NOIR_SUCC: got all symbols NOIR_PARTIAL: got all required symbols, but not all optional symbols NOIR_NOTFOUND: didn't get all of the required symbols NOIR_FAIL: invalid parameters NOIR_NODATA: caller asked for empty symbol name NOIR_NOFILE: couldn't open shared object NOIR_OOM: out of memory, symbol name too long

Parameters:
name - a logical name for the library, or NULL
file - the shared object; will be dlopen()ed and hence looked for in the usual places for shared objects (defined by ld.so.conf on linux)
flag - dlopen()-flags (RTLD_*)
libr - where to store the handle for the library
fmt - a space-separated list of symbols to try and load. symbols prefixed by '?' are optional, symbols prefixed by '!' are required.
... - where to store the function-pointers we get (or NULL for failure on an optional symbol)

generic quick-sort algorithm that hands user-data (sort-order, .

..) to the compare function and sorts pointers to the data rather than the data.

Parameters:
a - array of pointers to the data
data - user-data
lo - index of first element (0)
hi - index of last element (n-1)
compare - compare-function that takes pointers to user-data, first and second element and returns -1, 0, 1 for first element is "less than", "equal to", "greater than" the second element

void* timeout_add (  uint  f,
int(*)(void *)  fun,
void *  data
) 
 

delayed execution of a function.

the function will be executed every 'f' ms until it returns FALSE or is dequeued.

Returns:
a handle for the scheduled entry.
Parameters:
f - how long to wait before execution the function (ms)
fun - the function to call
data - user-data to hand to "fun" when it is called
